detailed_rationale:
Restaurant Brands Asia Ltd is the exclusive master franchisee for Burger King in India (~681 restaurants) and also runs Burger King and Popeyes in Indonesia through subsidiaries. Revenue growth has been steady (17.9% YoY in Q1 FY27 to Rs 698 crore, 11% TTM, 23% five-year CAGR), but the company has never achieved sustained net profitability at scale: Q1 FY27 posted a Rs 45 crore net loss and FY26 a Rs 204 crore net loss, with ROCE at -0.47% and three-year average ROE at -27%. High depreciation (Rs 389 crore) and interest costs (Rs 189 crore) on a capital-intensive, company-owned-restaurant model are the main drags, and promoter holding has fallen sharply, from 15.43% (Sep 2023) to just 9.22% now -- a real erosion of promoter conviction over time.

The development that changes the picture is very recent and material: in Q1 FY27, 'Inspira Global acquired a 42% stake and infused Rs 1,050 crore' into the company. A capital infusion and change-of-control event of this size is exactly the kind of structural shift that a backward-looking quant score (built on trailing financials) cannot see, and it could plausibly be either a genuine turnaround catalyst (fresh capital and possibly new operating discipline) or a signal that the prior ownership needed a rescue due to balance-sheet stress -- I do not have enough detail on Inspira Global's identity, stake structure or turnaround plan to distinguish between those two readings with confidence.

Reverse-DCF: on the standalone trailing numbers -- persistent net losses, negative ROCE, declining legacy promoter conviction, real leverage (Rs 1,967 crore borrowings) -- this looks like a Sell on fundamentals alone. But the fresh Rs 1,050 crore capital infusion and 42% new strategic stake is a large enough de-risking/ownership event, landing right at the point of scoring, that I think the call genuinely needs portfolio-manager-level judgment on what is actually intended by the new investor before treating this purely as a continuation of the old, loss-making trajectory.
recommendation_rationale: The core business remains loss-making with negative ROCE and a sharply eroded legacy promoter stake, which on its own supports the quant Sell. However, the Q1 FY27 entry of Inspira Global with a 42% stake and Rs 1,050 crore capital infusion is a material, very recent ownership/capital-structure change that predates and is not reflected in the quant score, and could meaningfully change the forward trajectory either way. I am keeping the recommendation at Sell (the proven financials are still weak) but flagging this for escalation given the genuine uncertainty a fresh change-of-control event introduces.
summary: Restaurant Brands Asia (Burger King India) continues to grow revenue but has not achieved sustained profitability, posting a net loss again this quarter and over the last full year, with a heavily reduced founding-promoter stake over time. A new investor, Inspira Global, has just taken a large 42% stake and injected Rs 1,050 crore of fresh capital -- a potentially significant development for the company's future that is too recent to fully assess. Based on the financials as they stand today we rate this a Sell, and flag the new-investor development for portfolio-manager review.
positive_para: Revenue continues to grow at a respectable double-digit pace (17.9% YoY latest quarter, 11% TTM), the Burger King brand has a genuine, sizeable store footprint (~681 restaurants) in India, and the fresh Rs 1,050 crore capital infusion from Inspira Global materially strengthens the balance sheet and could bring new operating focus to a chain that has struggled to convert scale into profit.
negative_para: The company has never shown sustained net profitability -- ROCE is negative (-0.47%) and three-year average ROE is -27%, driven by heavy depreciation and interest costs on a capital-intensive restaurant model -- and the original promoter's stake has collapsed from over 15% to just 9.2% over three years, a real erosion of founder conviction. Whether the new Inspira Global capital and ownership change actually fixes the underlying cost structure, versus simply refinancing an already-struggling balance sheet, is not yet demonstrated.
reverse_dcf_judgment: On trailing financials alone -- persistent losses, negative ROCE, declining legacy promoter stake, real leverage -- this does not clear a bar for holding. The wildcard is the Rs 1,050 crore Inspira Global capital infusion and 42% stake just this quarter, which is too fresh and too under-disclosed (from what I could verify) to confidently price as a turnaround; I am not crediting it as a reason to hold pending more clarity on the new investor's plans.
escalation_reason: Inspira Global's Q1 FY27 acquisition of a 42% stake plus a Rs 1,050 crore capital infusion is a material, very recent change-of-control/capital-structure event that the quant score (built on trailing financials) cannot reflect. It could be a genuine turnaround catalyst or a sign the prior ownership needed rescue capital -- I could not establish which from available sources, and recommend the PM/CIO review the new investor and deal terms directly before any final call on this position.
